algebraic_carriers.maps_to_algebra: ring with overflow (NOT a field; signed-overflow is UB per ISO C, unsigned wraps mod 2^N forming Z/2^NZ - which IS a commutative ring but not a field)
commutative_ring (Z/2^NZ - well-defined wrap; the canonical finite ring carrier in C)
field (approximation_of_field strictly; IEEE-754 single-precision, same caveats as Python float)
monoid (degenerate - struct is a product type; the substrate's monoid card carries the product-type representative until a product_type / cartesian algebra card lands in W22)
monoid (null-terminated string concatenation via strcat; pointer arithmetic semantics distinct from the operation)

flaws: int-not-ring: signed integer overflow is UB in ISO C, so 'int' is *not* a ring under the strict definition (the operation isn't total). The 'ring with overflow' label is a substrate convention; a rigorous fix would split into 'signed_int_with_UB' (no algebra at all) vs. unsigned (commutative_ring). W22 follow-up.

struct-is-product-not-monoid: 'monoid' is honestly a placeholder; struct is a product type and the substrate lacks a product_type / cartesian_algebra card. W22 follow-up: add cards/algebra/product_type/card.json and retarget.
weak-typing: 'weak' is a coarse label - C permits implicit numeric conversions and void* casts but rejects most truly-arbitrary coercions. A finer-grained 'coercion_lattice' field is a W23+ idea.

C-frontend-subset: the linked c.py frontend covers ~80% of typical-coreutils C, not the full grammar - this card describes the LANGUAGE, not the substrate's parser coverage. Coverage gaps are tracked in c.py docstring.
informal_description: C is a weakly-but-statically-typed imperative/procedural language with eager evaluation, fully permissive side effects, and explicit manual memory management via malloc/free. C exposes the machine: raw pointers, integer overflow (UB for signed, modular for unsigned), bit-level control of struct layout, and inline assembly. Concurrency was bolted on by POSIX (pthreads) and standardised in C11 (<threads.h>, <stdatomic.h>) - the original language had none. C int is a ring with overflow (signed: UB; unsigned: Z/2^NZ); float/double approximate a field. struct is a product type; array decay and pointer arithmetic break the abstraction barrier so C's type system is genuinely weak (no automatic coercion safety, no array-bounds checking, void* erases types). The transpile frontend at cards/tool/v_transpile/frontends/c.py is a regex-+-recursive-descent subset parser sufficient for typical leaf coreutils (cat, echo, true, false, sleep, ...) plus the UB4-D extensions (macros, function pointers, bit fields, designated initialisers). It does NOT parse the full C grammar - constructs outside the supported subset lift as raw nodes.
name: c
notes: C89/C99/C11/C17/C23 - this card describes the abstract language ~C11 (which standardised threads and atomics). The substrate's c.py frontend supports a working subset, not the full grammar.
